source.name: sp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT = 10
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT DEFAULT 10
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName VARCHAR,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The 'dbo' schema exists in PostgreSQL or should be created
CustomerID column is of type INT in both Customers and Orders tables
FirstName and LastName are VARCHAR or TEXT types
TotalAmount is a numeric type (NUMERIC, DECIMAL, or similar)
OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) is converted to EXTRACT(DAY FROM ...) which may have slight behavioral differences with NULL handling
String concatenation using + is converted to || operator

reviewFlags.reason: DATEDIFF behavior differs from PostgreSQL date arithmetic. SQL Server DATEDIFF counts date boundaries crossed, while PostgreSQL EXTRACT returns the difference in days as a decimal. For customers with no orders (MAX(o.OrderDate) is NULL), SQL Server returns NULL while PostgreSQL will also return NULL, but the calculation method differs for non-NULL values.
Column data types (VARCHAR, NUMERIC) are generic. Review actual table schema to specify precise types like VARCHAR(100), NUMERIC(18,2), etc. for better type safety and performance.
Verify that TOP N behavior matches LIMIT N in all edge cases, particularly when p_TopN is NULL, 0, or negative. SQL Server may handle these differently.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server procedure converted to PostgreSQL function because it returns a result set. Calling syntax changes from EXEC/EXECUTE to SELECT * FROM function_name(params).

DATEDIFF(DAY, date1, date2) counts the number of day boundaries crossed. PostgreSQL date subtraction returns an interval, and EXTRACT(DAY FROM interval) returns the day component. Results may differ by 1 day in some cases, especially around daylight saving time boundaries.

SQL Server + operator converted to PostgreSQL || operator. Both handle NULL differently: SQL Server returns NULL if any operand is NULL, PostgreSQL CONCAT-like behavior requires COALESCE if NULL handling is critical.
GETDATE() returns DATETIME without timezone. CURRENT_TIMESTAMP returns TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. Consider using CURRENT_DATE or LOCALTIMESTAMP if timezone-aware behavior is not desired.
COUNT behavior is identical, but ensure SUM with COALESCE handles empty groups correctly. Both databases return NULL for SUM of empty set, wrapped by COALESCE to 0.
